Subject: SLA concern / request for A/B hold + automated rollback

Hi Sofia / Priyom,

Quick background: we start A/B next week for the BrightLeaf search assistant. Legal asked for an explicit SLA mitigation clause while we run the experiment — they want to ensure customer-facing latency doesn’t regress during the A/B window. Our legal and ops teams are asking: can Redwood authorize a temporary release hold (pin the control at the production-verified model) and enable an automated rollback to baseline if latency or error metrics cross thresholds?

Key asks:
- Temporary pin + hold for the A/B cohort if we see latency regressions.
- Automatic fallback to baseline version when telemetry gate trips (p95 latency and error rate).
- A form we can sign to record the exception (Legal).

I attached a short telemetry extract (telemetry-sample.csv) showing some pre-release p95 numbers — nothing catastrophic but we want the safety net.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide that level of control and the exact conditions you’d need to authorize the rollback? If there are cost or SLA carveouts we need to be aware of, flag them now.

Thanks,
Pete

Pete — thanks for the clear ask and the sample. We can support a documented hold + automated rollback as an SLA mitigation for the duration of your A/B. Below is the operational proposal from our side; if this matches your legal/ops needs we’ll prepare the SLA-exception-form and loop in Ben for commercial sign-off.

Operational proposal (summary):
- Scoped duration: A/B window up to 14 days (extendable by mutual agreement).
- Pin: We will pin the control cohort to your currently verified model SHA (you provide model tag).
- Auto-fallback trigger (any of the following sustained for > 10 minutes):
  - p95 latency increase > 250ms absolute OR > 30% relative vs. baseline
  - user-facing error rate increase > 1% absolute
  - sustained token-cost delta > 20% (ops safety check)
- Action on trigger: immediate routing shift of affected cohort back to pinned baseline model + traffic rebalancing (no manual approval required).
- Observability: we’ll stream telemetry to your project channel (and retain a 30-day incident trace). We’ll also post an automated incident to the Console and create a rollback event in the rollout history.
- Canary sizing: recommend 10% initial A/B cohort, ramp up to 25% over 48h after health checks pass.
- KV cache warming: we’ll pre-warm caches for pinned model to avoid cold-start p95 spikes (requires 2 hours pre-warm).

Conditions & Caveats:
- This is an operational exception tied to the A/B experiment only; it does not change baseline SLA terms beyond the documented mitigation.
- Any additional dedicated capacity or larger canary sizes may change committed throughput guarantees — we’ll surface cost impacts in the exception form.

Next steps:
1) Priyom — can you confirm the telemetry gate thresholds are implementable from the runtime side?
2) If yes, I’ll prepare the SLA-exception-form (PDF) for BrightLeaf signature and loop in Ben for commercial approval.

—

This is implementable. A few implementation notes and suggested tweaks from the runtime side:
- Telemetry windows: use rolling 10-minute windows with 1-minute granularity to avoid noisy short spikes. Trigger requires 3 consecutive 1-minute windows above threshold before we escalate the 10-minute sustained condition.
- p95 gating: we’ll compare to the 72-hour trailing baseline (not single-run baseline) to avoid false-positives during low-traffic hours.
- Error-rate: distinguish between client-originated 4xx vs. server 5xx; auto-fallback should only consider 5xx+internal error types.
- Safety net: when fallback occurs we’ll automatically hold new rollouts for 1 hour and throttle any re-ramp for 24 hours until manual review.
- Ops hooks: we’ll emit a "rollback_intent" trace and an "rollback_executed" event; include these in the incident body so BR team can correlate with their logs.

Attachment: I’ll include the telemetry gating YAML in the exception form; that will be machine-readable for our router.
